text:
Offline voice interaction
with persistent memory
Introduce Nova as an offline-first personal voice companion. Today's live demonstration uses Windows. Raspberry Pi deployment remains under physical validation.
A voice companion that remembers useful information and helps manage everyday work.
Say Nova to ask a question, save a note, or manage a task or reminder.
Speech recognition, language inference, speech synthesis and SQLite storage run locally.
Windows development today. Raspberry Pi 5 with 4 GB RAM as the deployment target.
The original goal was a 24-hour hackathon prototype. Explain the intended need without claiming market statistics or medical benefits. Source: project handoff and current user discussion.
Microphone capture and voice activity detection feed local Whisper.cpp transcription.
Wake detection routes active commands to the assistant, local tools or Ollama.
SQLite stores confirmed facts, observations, notes, tasks and reminders.
Piper generates speech. The default mode returns to listening after playback.

Explain each layer in order. Whisper.cpp transcribes audio, wake detection activates supported requests, and deterministic tools handle memory and scheduling. Ollama handles general conversation and Piper speaks. Sources: scripts/always_on_assistant.py and project stack.

Wake detection
Active or passive routing

Optional background speech
Bounded queue and grounding

Memory tools and loopback Ollama
Optional weather and news tools

Local SQLite
Facts, observations, notes, tasks, reminders
Privacy and cancellation controls apply across the runtime. Online tools require explicit opt-in.

Read the top row left to right. All captured speech passes the software mute gate before transcription. Wake detection routes active commands through Assistant and QueryRouter. Optional non-wake speech enters a bounded passive queue and grounding processor with no spoken reply. Active tools save and retrieve SQLite records. General conversation uses loopback-only Ollama. The scheduler supplies due reminders to the voice output loop. Piper synthesis and speaker playback complete active responses. Controls apply across the runtime. Online weather and news are explicit opt-in exceptions and receive no memory or history. Sources: scripts/always_on_assistant.py; core/assistant.py; memory/passive_worker.py; memory/passive_processor.py; router/query_router.py; tools/online_tools.py. Pi hardware validation remains pending.
Continuous listening, wake activation, local conversation and spoken responses.
Confirmed facts, optional passive observations, paraphrased recall and memory review.
Persistent notes, task completion and editing, reminder scheduling and rescheduling.
Software mute, confirmed deletion, privacy filtering and optional interruption.

These are implemented software capabilities. Avoid claiming all have just passed physical testing. Explicit memory and hello worked in the latest user demonstration. Sources: docs/TASKS_AND_REMINDERS.md, docs/PRIVACY.md and user confirmation.
Half-duplex operation preserves the established listening and playback behavior.
Passive extraction and experimental console or spoken interruption use configuration flags.
Open-Meteo weather and NewsAPI headlines require explicit online enablement.
ARM64 setup, model provisioning, GPIO controls and systemd startup are implemented.

Keep the working defaults for evaluation. Online providers require explicit opt-in. Experimental interruption has echo limitations. GPIO and service preparation do not establish real hardware success. Sources: config and deployment documentation.
Grounding rejects negation, questions, hypotheticals and unsupported task or event claims.
Ollama accepts loopback endpoints. External tools stay disabled by default.
Credential checks, sanitized diagnostics, temporary audio cleanup and optional retention.
Mute boundaries, bounded queues, accepted-work draining and confirmed record changes.
Describe these as safeguards implemented and regression-tested, not guarantees of flawless real-world operation. Sources: module history 12.7.1 through 12.9 and docs/PRIVACY.md.
Some live voice attempts miss an answer. Commands need clear speech and completion time.
The recent passive attempt saved no memories. Demo reliability still needs validation.
Speaker-only playback works. Microphone recordings still produce static.
Physical GPIO and systemd tests, extended reliability runs, and live provider tests remain.

Be transparent: the recent passive extraction produced five rejected suggestions and zero saves. Active voice sometimes misses an answer. Bluetooth standalone output worked but recorded microphone audio contained static on Pi. Multi-hour physical soak remains deferred.
Run Nova on the tested Windows setup while showing the Raspberry Pi prototype separately.
Hello and favorite-food saving and recall worked in the latest live test.
Greeting, explicit memory, note, task, reminder, mute and recall after restart.
Keep a local recording of a successful run. Avoid new installations during evaluation.

The user confirmed hello and favorite-food saving and recall worked. Do not describe the remaining sequence as already performed. Present it as the live demonstration plan. Source: latest conversation.

Nova, my favorite food is biryani.
Nova, what is my favorite food?

Nova, remember that the demo is in room seven.
Nova, add a task to finish my project.
Nova, remind me to drink water in 1 minute.
Press M to test mute. Unmute, restart, then recall the saved favorite food.

Say one command at a time. Wait for LISTENING. Say Nova, yes only when asked for confirmation. Do not repeat writes blindly if playback fails. Replace task IDs with IDs that Nova actually returns. Sources: current command checklist and supported router documentation.
Capture project notes and create reminders for study sessions or deadlines.
Manage project tasks and recall preferences without switching to a keyboard.
Save explicitly requested facts and receive reminders for ordinary activities.
Use local voice and memory after provisioning without a cloud inference service.
These are intended applications of implemented features, not measured outcomes. Nova is not a medical, financial or safety-critical assistant.
Confirmed facts take priority. Passive observations preserve speaker attribution.
Corrections and destructive actions require confirmation and scoped record selection.
Data stays local, but local storage alone does not guarantee encryption or secure erasure.
GPIO mute controls software capture. Pi audio and hardware validation remain pending.

SQLite deletion is not secure erasure and local storage does not imply encryption at rest. Software mute is not an electrical microphone cutoff. Never treat an unknown passive speaker as the owner. No real Pi deployment validation claim.

Nova
Offline voice interaction with persistent memory
Invite questions and offer the live demonstration. Reiterate that the validated software demo is on Windows and Raspberry Pi microphone audio remains unresolved.
